acf.introduction: The SPECS Scheme focuses on enhancing electronics components manufacturing in India, providing a 25% financial incentive on capital expenditure to electronic components and semiconductor/display units.
acf.eligibility: Applicable to Investments in New Units as well as Expansion of Existing Units
acf.l3_introduction: The Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) aims to offset the disability for domestic manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors in order to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the country. Submit SPECS applications: Link

components.component_description: Development of supply chain is essential for the manufacturing of electronic products with higher domestic value addition. The vision of National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019) is to position India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) by encouraging and driving capabilities in the country for developing core components, including chipsets, and creating an enabling environment for the industry to compete globally. Electronic components are the basic building blocks for Electronics Industry and entail maximum value addition. Therefore, a vibrant electronic components manufacturing ecosystem is vital for the overall long-term and sustainable growth of electronics manufacturing in India and essential to achieve net positive Balance of Payments (BoP). The Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) notified vide Gazette Notification No.CG-DL-E-01042020-218992 dated April 01, 2020 will help offset the disability for domestic manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors in order to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The scheme will provide financial incentive of 25% on capital expenditure for the identified list of electronic goods that comprise downstream value chain of electronic products, i.e., electronic components, semiconductor/ display fabrication units, ATMP units, specialized sub-assemblies and capital goods for manufacture of aforesaid goods, all of which involve high value added manufacturing. The Scheme will be applicable to investments in new units and expansion of capacity/ modernization and diversification of existing units.  Application under the Scheme can be made by any entity registered in India. The capital expenditure will be total of expenditure in plant, machinery, equipment, associated utilities and technology, including for Research & Development (R&D). The Scheme is open for applications initially for 3 years from the date of its notification. Incentives under the Scheme will be applicable from the date of acknowledgment of the application. The incentives will be available for investment made within 5 years from the date of acknowledgement of application. The Scheme will be implemented through a nodal agency which will act as Project Management Agency (PMA) and be responsible for providing secretarial, managerial and implementation support and carrying out other responsibilities as assigned by MeitY from time to time.

title.rendered: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing

acf.scheme_title: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
acf.introduction: Our Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing is designed to provide a financial boost for domestic manufacturing and attract significant investments in the electronics value chain, covering electronic components and semiconductor packaging.
acf.l3_introduction:
The domestic electronics hardware manufacturing sector faces lack of a level playing field vis-à-vis competing nations. The sector suffers disability of around 8.5% to 11% on account of lack of adequate infrastructure, domestic supply chain and logistics; high cost of finance; inadequate availability of quality power; limited design capabilities and focus on R&D by the industry; and inadequacies in skill development. The vision of National Policy on Electronics 2019 (NPE 2019) is to position India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) by encouraging and driving capabilities in the country for developing core components and creating an enabling environment for the industry to compete globally. Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing notified vide Gazette Notification No.CG-DL-E-01042020-218990 dated April 01, 2020 offers a production linked incentive to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments in mobile phone manufacturing and specified electronic components, including Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) units. The Scheme would tremendously boost the electronics manufacturing landscape and establish India at the global level in electronics sector. The scheme shall extend an incentive of 4% to 6% on incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India and covered under target segments, to eligible companies, for a period of five (5) years subsequent to the base year as defined. The Scheme is open for applications for a period of 4 months initially which may be extended. Support under the Scheme shall be provided for a period of five (5) years subsequent to the base year The Scheme will be implemented through a Nodal Agency which shall act as a  Project Management Agency (PMA) and be responsible for providing secretarial, managerial and implementation support and carrying out other responsibilities as assigned by MeitY from time to time.

Second Round of the Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing

After the success of the First Round of Production Linked Incentive Scheme in attracting investments in mobile phone and electronic component manufacturing, the proposal for accepting applications under Second Round of the PLI Scheme has been approved by the Competent Authority. The target segment for the purpose of this round shall be Specified Electronic Components. Under the Second Round, incentives of 5% to 3% shall be extended on incremental sales (over base year i.e. 2019-20) of goods manufactured in India and covered under the target segment, to eligible companies, for a period of four (4) years. The Application Window was open until 31.03.2021. Incentives under the Second Round of PLI Scheme shall be applicable from 01.04.2021.

acf.scheme_title: Production Linked Incentive Scheme – PLI 2.0 for IT Hardware
acf.introduction: The PLI 2.0 Scheme aims to boost domestic manufacturing, attract significant investments in the value chain and incentivise semiconductor design, IC manufacturing, and packaging by providing production-linked incentives.
acf.eligibility: Global and domestic companies manufacturing IT hardware in India
acf.l3_introduction:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has given its approval to introduce the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware for Enhancing India’s Manufacturing Capabilities and Enhancing Exports – Atmanirbhar Bharat on 17.05.2023

Production Linked Incentive Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware notified vide Gazette Notification No. CG-DL-E-30052023-246165 dated May 29, 2023 offers a production linked incentive to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments in the value chain.

The PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware is expected to result in broadening and deepening of the manufacturing ecosystem by encouraging the localisation of components and sub-assemblies and allowing for a longer duration to develop the supply chain within the country. Additionally, the scheme provides increased flexibility and options for applicants, and is tied to incremental sales and investment thresholds to further incentivise growth. Furthermore, semiconductor design, IC manufacturing, and packaging are also included as incentivized components of the PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware.

The Scheme shall extend an average incentive of around 5% on net incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India and covered under the target segment, to eligible companies, for a period of six (6) years. The Target Segment under PLI shall include (i) Laptops (ii) Tablets (iii) All-in-One PCs (iv) Servers and Ultra Small Form Factor (USFF).

Support under the Scheme shall be provided to companies based on the eligibility criteria laid down, for manufacturing of goods (covered under the target segment) in India.

acf.l3_introduction:
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India initiated “Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT” in the year 2014 with an objective to enhance the number of PhDs in Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (IT/ITES) sectors in the country.

“Phase-II of the Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT” was launched in 2021 for a period of nine years with a total estimated cost of Rs. 481.93 crore.

To achieve the above objectives, 1016 Full Time and 330 Part Time PhD candidates were enrolled at eligible institutions across the country under Phase-I of the scheme. Further, 158 Young Faculty Research Fellowships (YFRFs) were awarded. Under Phase-II of the scheme, 1000 Full Time and 153 Part Time PhD seats have been allotted to the eligible institutions. The details of EOU/EHTP schemes are available in Chapter-6 of India’s Foreign Trade Policy and Procedures on the website of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry. Details pertaining to SEZ scheme are also available on this website.

The Zero duty EPCG Scheme is available to exporters of electronic products. It allows import of capital goods for pre-production, production and post-production (including CKD/SKD thereof as well as computer software systems) at zero% customs duty, subject to an export obligation equivalent to 6 times of duty saved on capital goods imported under EPCG scheme, to be fulfilled in 6 years reckoned from Authorization issue-date.

Duty exemption schemes enable duty free import of inputs required for export production. Duty exemption schemes consist of:

  • Duty Free Import Authorization (DFIA) scheme

  • Duty Drawback (DBK) Scheme
The details of these schemes are available in Chapter-4 of India’s Foreign Trade Policy and Procedures on the website of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry (https://commerce.gov.in/)

"Deemed Exports" refer to those transactions in which the goods supplied do not leave the country, and the payment for such supplies is received either in Indian rupees or in free foreign exchange. The following categories of supply of goods by the main/ sub-contractors are regarded as "Deemed Exports" under the Foreign Trade Policy, provided the goods are manufactured in India:
  1. Supply of goods against Advance Authorization/Advance Authorization for annual requirement/DFIA
  2. Supply of goods to Export Oriented Units (EOUs) / Software Technology Park (STP) units / Electronic Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) units / Biotechnology Park (BTP) units
  3. Supply of capital goods to Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Authorization holders
  4. Supply of goods to projects financed by multilateral or bilateral Agencies/Funds as notified by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance under International Competitive Bidding (ICB) in accordance with the procedures of those Agencies/Funds, where the legal agreements provide for tender evaluation without including customs duty
  5. Supply of capital goods, including in unassembled/disassembled condition as well as plants, machinery, accessories, tools, dies and such goods which are used for installation purposes till the stage of commercial production, and spares to the extent of 10% of the FOR value to fertilizer plants
  6. Supply of goods to any project or purpose in respect of which the Ministry of Finance, by a notification, permits the import of such goods at zero customs duty
  7. Supply of goods to the power projects and refineries not covered in (6) above
Supply of marine freight containers by 100% EOU (Domestic freight containers - manufacturers) provided the said containers are exported out of India within 6 months or such further period as permitted by the customs:
  • Supply to projects funded by UN agencies
  • Supply of goods to nuclear power projects through competitive bidding as opposed to ICB.
The benefits of deemed exports shall be available under paragraph (4), (5), (6) and (7) only if the supply is made under the procedure of ICB.

Deemed exports shall be eligible for any/all of the following benefits in respect of manufacture and supply of goods qualifying as deemed exports subject to the terms and conditions as given in the Chapter-8 of Handbook of Procedures (Vol. I), 2009-2014 of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry:
  • Advance Authorization/Advance Authorization for annual requirement/DFIA
  • Deemed Export Drawback.
  • Exemption from terminal excise duty where supplies are made against ICB. In other cases, refund of terminal excise duty will be given.
The details of “Deemed Exports” scheme are available in Chapter-8 of India’s Foreign Trade Policy and Procedures on the website of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

acf.scheme_title: BPO promotion Schemes
acf.introduction: The India BPO Promotion Scheme (IBPS) and North-East BPO Promotion Scheme (NEBPS) aims to foster youth employment by providing Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to eligible companies, encouraging investments in the IT/ITeS industry as well as establishing BPO/ITeS operations in smaller cities.
acf.l3_introduction:
Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India notified the “India BPO Promotion Scheme (IBPS)” and “Northeast BPO Promotion Scheme (NEBPS)” under Digital India Programme. The schemes provide financial support in the form of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to eligible companies, with the following objectives:

• Creation of employment opportunities for the youth, by promoting the IT/ITeS Industry particularly by setting up the BPO/ITeS operations in smaller cities.

acf.scheme_title: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
acf.introduction: The IT Hardware manufacturing sector faces the lack of a level playing field vis-à-vis competing nations. As per industry estimates (Source: ICEA and ELCINA), electronics manufacturing sector suffers from a disability of around 8.5% to 11% on account of lack of adequate infrastructure, domestic supply chain and logistics
acf.l3_introduction: The IT Hardware manufacturing sector faces the lack of a level playing field vis-à-vis competing nations. As per industry estimates (Source: ICEA and ELCINA), electronics manufacturing sector suffers from a disability of around 8.5% to 11% on account of lack of adequate infrastructure, domestic supply chain and logistics; high cost of finance; inadequate availability of quality power; limited design capabilities and focus on R&D by the industry; and inadequacies in skill development. There is need for a mechanism to compensate for the manufacturing disabilities vis-à-vis other major manufacturing economies. The vision of NPE 2019 is to position India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) by encouraging and driving capabilities in the country for developing core components, including chipsets, and creating an enabling environment for the industry to compete globally. Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware notified vide Gazette Notification No. CG-DL-E-03032021-225613 dated March 03, 2021 offers a production linked incentive to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments in the value chain. The Scheme shall extend an incentive of 4% to 2% / 1% on net incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India and covered under the target segment, to eligible companies, for a period of four (4) years. The Target Segment under PLI shall include (i) Laptops (ii) Tablets (iii) All-in-One PCs and (iv) Servers. Support under the Scheme shall be provided to companies based on the eligibility criteria laid down, for manufacturing of goods (covered under the target segment) in India. The Scheme will be implemented through a Nodal Agency which shall act as a Project Management Agency (PMA) and be responsible for providing secretarial, managerial and implementation support and carrying out other responsibilities as assigned by MeitY from time to time.

acf.scheme_title: Scheme of financial assistance for setting up of Electronics and ICT Academies
acf.introduction: The Electronics and IT sector is characterized by fastest emergence of new technologies leading to high rate of obsolescence leaving very short response time to absorb the technology, adopt the same and evolve new technologies/solutions.
acf.l3_introduction:
The Electronics and IT sector is characterized by fastest emergence of new technologies leading to high rate of obsolescence leaving very short response time to absorb the technology, adopt the same and evolve new technologies/solutions. In addition, electronics is characterized by high velocity technology change leading to declining life cycle of products. Further, IECT is increasingly finding applications in all sectors of economy and is a key enabler in development of a country. Keeping in view the above requirements, MeitY in November, 2014 had approved a scheme entitled “Scheme of Financial Assistance for setting up of Electronics and ICT Academies” for faculty/mentor development/ up-gradation to improve the employability of the students in engineering/ other streams. As per the Scheme approval, Seven (07) Electronics and ICT academies have been set up and are operational at 7 premier and leading academic institutions viz. (i) NIT Warangal (Telangana), (ii) IIITDM Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), (iii) IIT Guwahati (Assam), (iv) NIT Patna (Bihar), (v) IIT Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), (vi) IIT Roorkee (Uttarakhand) and (vii) MNIT Jaipur (Rajasthan). The total target under the scheme is to train 92,800 Faculties. Each Academy is expected to generate revenue by charging fee and taking up other activities and become self-sustainable at the end of the project. The scheme would lead to enhancement of the skills of the students in the Electronics and ICT sector. The Ministry had earlier setup two ICT Academies in Tamil Nadu and Kerala respectively. Objective of Each Academy:
  • To focus on improving the quality of faculty of institutes, colleges in the respective states/UTs by organising faculty training programmes
    • Engineering, Polytechnics etc in emerging areas of electronics & IT;
    • Arts, Commerce & Science colleges, etc on utilisation of IT tools and techniques for application in their respective domain of knowledge/learning/teaching/enhancing productivity
  • To develop state-of-the-art facilities like technical labs, well equipped library, interactive virtual learning facility, etc.
As per the original scheme approval, the total outlay of the scheme was Rs 147.48 crores with duration of 5 years. With the approval of the competent authority the scheme has been extended upto 31.03.2022 (total duration 7 years & 5 months) with the revised outlay of Rs. 87.69 Crore and duration of the scheme has been revised. acf.l3_introduction:
Telecom Centres of Excellence India (TCOE India) would like to inform that the Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), Department of Telecommunications (DoT), has invited applications for the Reimbursement of Testing and Certification Charges for Start-ups and Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs) in the telecom sector. Interested applicants can submit their applications through the online portal https://tec.gov.in/tcrs starting from March 10, 2025.

Overview

Testing and certification of telecom equipment are essential for Start-ups and MSEs to ensure compliance with national and international standards, enhancing consumer confidence, driving business growth, and facilitating market adoption. To support this, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has introduced a reimbursement scheme that covers a portion of the testing and certification costs incurred under mandatory or voluntary certification schemes.

Under this scheme, Start-ups and MSEs can claim reimbursement for testing and certification expenses incurred at TEC/NCCS-designated or recognized labs or NABL-accredited labs (where no TEC-designated Conformity Assessment Body (CAB) exists for a specific test facility).

Reimbursement Criteria:' Reimbursement will be provided based on the following structure:

  • Start-ups: 75% of testing & certification charges
  • Micro Enterprises: 60% of testing & certification charges
  • Small Enterprises: 50% of testing & certification charges

Scheme Duration

The scheme will be operational for two years from the date of implementation or until funds of ₹25 crores allocated from TTDF, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) are fully utilized, whichever occurs earlier. A Max of ₹50 Lakhs per entity can be reimbursed.

Further details and scheme implementation guidelines are attached for your reference.

We kindly request your support in sharing this opportunity within your networks—via internal mailing lists, newsletters, or social media—to help us reach a broader community of innovators. Your outreach can empower promising ventures and strengthen the national telecom ecosystem.

acf_data.l3_introduction:
The Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF) was launched by the Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile Universal Service Obligation Fund) under the Ministry of Communications on 1 October 2022 to promote indigenous research, development, innovation and commercialization in the telecom sector. The Scheme seeks to accelerate the development of next-generation communication technologies by fostering collaboration among start-ups, MSMEs, industry, academia and research institutions, thereby strengthening India’s telecom innovation ecosystem and reducing dependence on imported technologies.

As on 31.03.2026, telecom R&D projects with sanctioned funding of nearly ₹500 crore have been approved and are at various stages of implementation. The approved projects span a broad spectrum of frontier technologies, including 6G technologies such as THz systems, AI/ML-enabled networks, advanced radio access technologies and next-generation communication architectures; 5G technologies covering indigenous core networks, transceivers and radio-frequency components; quantum communication focusing on secure communication and encryption technologies; optical communication encompassing advanced fibre systems, optical networking components and high-capacity transmission technologies; and satellite communications, including technologies for non-terrestrial networks, satellite payloads, navigation systems and drone-based applications. These projects contribute towards building an indigenous, secure, resilient and globally competitive telecom technology ecosystem.

Salient Features:

(a) Promotion of indigenous telecom research, development and innovation in strategic and emerging technology areas.

(b) Financial support for telecom R&D projects undertaken by start-ups, MSMEs, industry, academia and research institutions.

(c) Encouragement of collaborative research involving industry-academia partnerships.

(d) Support for development, testing, prototyping, validation and commercialization of telecom technologies and products.

(e) Focus on next-generation technologies including 5G, 6G, quantum communications, satellite communications, optical communications, artificial intelligence and telecom security.

(f) Promotion of intellectual property creation, standards participation and technology commercialization.

(g) Strengthening of India’s capabilities in strategic telecom technologies and enhancement of technological self-reliance.

Duration of the Scheme/Project:

The Scheme was launched on 1 October 2022 during the Fifteenth Finance Commission cycle and is being continued during the Sixteenth Finance Commission cycle to facilitate the completion of projects approved under the Scheme. Since the approved financial outlay has been fully committed, no fresh projects are presently being sanctioned. The approved projects, which generally have implementation timelines of two to four years, continue to be supported and monitored as per their approved milestones and implementation schedules.

acf_data.l3_introduction:
The TDIP Scheme is a Central Sector scheme aimed at positioning India as a global leader in telecom innovation, standardisation, and exports. The scheme builds on India’s strong digital foundation and supports the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, National Digital Commissions Policy (NDCP) 2018, and the nation’s 6G ambitions. Its aim to transform India into a globally competitive and self-reliant hub for telecom technology development, standardisation, and exports by fostering a synergistic ecosystem of industry, startups, and R&D institutions.

Salient Features:  

The objectives and key activities of the scheme are to strengthen India’s participation in global telecom standardisation, foster ecosystem innovation, incubation, and commercialisation, and ensure operational excellence along with the evolution of labs/testbed infrastructure. It also promotes active participation in global standardisation bodies such as the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), and oneM2M. Support is provided for memberships, international participation, and hosting global telecom events in India. The annual activities under the scheme will primarily be executed by the Telecommunications Standards Development Society, India (TSDSI), Telecommunications Consultants India Limited (TCIL), and Telecom Centres of Excellence (TCoE) India. The scheme will be implemented with a total financial outlay of Rs. 203 crore over a five-year period from 2026–27 to 2030–31. 

Duration of the Scheme/Project: 

The scheme spans five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-2031.

Telecom Centres of Excellence India (TCOE India) invites applications from eligible DPIIT-recognized Startups and Udyam-registered MSMEs under the Technology Development & Investment Promotion (TDIP) Program. The Program offers financial assistance of up to ₹50 lakh per project (up to 80% of the approved project cost) for prototyping, Proof-of-Concept (PoC), validation, and pilot deployments of telecom and ICT solutions at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 5–8.

For the Program Guidelines, eligibility criteria, FAQs, and online application submission, please visit https://pilot.tcoe.in.

The scheme provides financial assistance of up to 80% of eligible travel expenses, subject to a maximum of ₹5 lakh per person per international 3GPP Working Group/TSG meeting, to promote India’s participation in global telecom standardization activities.

acf_data.l3_introduction:
Testing and certification of telecom equipment are key enabler for Start-ups and telecom MSE’s, to ensure acceptance at both national and international deployment. Certificated products/solutions build consumer confidence and drive business growth, fostering adoption in domestic and global markets.

In order to support Start-ups and Micro & Small Enterprises (MSE’s), the competent authority has decided to reimburse testing and certification charges for Start-ups and MSEs in respect of testing and certification in the field of telecom under mandatory/voluntary testing certification scheme.

Objectives of the Scheme:

To reimburse a part of the testing and certification charges for Start-ups and MSEs in the field of telecom/ICT incurred by them at Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC)/ National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) designated/ recognized labs or at NABL accredited Lab(s) [in case there is no TEC designated CAB for a particular test facility] under mandatory/voluntary testing certification scheme.

To increase the competence of Start-ups/ MSE’s and create a conducive ecosystem in Telecom product development thereby promoting their competitiveness in the domestic and export markets.

Reimbursement Process:

The reimbursement process is streamlined through the online application portal.

Eligibility for reimbursements:

In order to be eligible for reimbursement under the Testing & Certification Scheme, Start-ups should have valid registration with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India in the Start-Up category.

In order to be eligible for reimbursement under the scheme, the MSEs firms shall have valid registration with Ministry of MSME, either in Micro or Small Category.

Start-up/ MSE’s annual revenue should not have crossed INR 5 crores in any financial year (since incorporation) and the Start-up should not have raised funds more than INR 10 crores.

Reimbursement Criterion:

The reimbursement of testing done at Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) / National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) designated/ recognized labs or at NABL accredited Lab(s) [in case there is no TEC designated CAB for a particular test facility] in India & certification charges will be made as per the below mentioned categorization:

Category Reimbursement of Testing and certification charges up to (in %)
Start- Ups 75
Micro Enterprises 60
Small Enterprises 50

acf_data.introduction: Nestled at the pivotal crossroads of Delhi and Gurgaon in Dwarka, New Delhi, Yashobhoomi ( India International Convention and Exhibition Centre Limited – IICCL ) stands as a beacon of innovation and sophistication in India’s event management landscape.
acf_data.l3_introduction:
Welcome to Yashobhoomi: India’s Largest and Most Advanced Convention & Exhibition Centre

Introducing Yashobhoomi

Nestled at the pivotal crossroads of Delhi and Gurgaon in Dwarka, New Delhi, Yashobhoomi ( India International Convention and Exhibition Centre Limited – IICCL ) stands as a beacon of innovation and sophistication in India’s event management landscape. With its groundbreaking infrastructure and strategic location, Yashobhoomi is poised to redefine the standards for hosting large-scale national and international events.

On September 17, 2023, Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first phase of Yashobhoomi. Developed at a cost of ₹5,400 crore and spread across 8.9 lakh square meters, this world-class facility includes multiple exhibition halls, meeting rooms, and a grand convention centre with a seating capacity of over 11,000 delegates.

Experience Modernity Interwoven with Tradition

Yashobhoomi is not just a venue; it embodies India’s dedication to excellence in infrastructure and hospitality. Designed to accommodate a diverse range of activities—from global conventions to trade exhibitions, cultural showcases, and corporate gatherings—Yashobhoomi offers an exceptional experience tailored to the needs of its users. Our facilities seamlessly blend cutting-edge technology with traditional hospitality, ensuring that every event conducted here leaves an indelible mark on attendees and organizers alike.

India’s Premier Convention and Exhibition Hub

Set to become the largest convention and exhibition centre in the country upon the completion of its Phase 2 development, Yashobhoomi is envisioned as a mega-complex ready to host your grandest events. Key features include:

  • Five Expansive Exhibition Halls: Perfectly designed for grand displays and versatile configurations that adapt to your event’s requirements.
  • Multi-Purpose Convention Centre: Home to India’s largest auditorium, comfortably seating 6,000 attendees, ensuring ample space for large assemblies and presentations.
  • Capacity for 20,000 Attendees: Facilities developed with a proactive approach, capable of accommodating large audiences, boosting engagement, and fostering connections.

In addition to these remarkable features, Yashobhoomi is surrounded by well-planned infrastructure, including 3,500 hotel rooms situated within a one-kilometre radius, shopping centres, entertainment zones, and office spaces. This makes Yashobhoomi a one-stop destination, catering to the varied needs of event organizers, exhibitors, and visitors alike.

Exceptional Location and Accessibility

Yashobhoomi’s prime location is one of its standout features. Just 10 km away from Indira Gandhi International Airport, it is strategically positioned for both domestic and international guests. Being 25 km from the bustling heart of New Delhi, the centre is easily accessible with minimal traffic congestion, facilitating smooth transit for all who attend. Nearby attractions such as a state-of-the-art sports complex, diplomatic residences, and a vibrant golf course enhance the appeal of Yashobhoomi as a premier event destination. Additionally, an airport city hotel offers luxurious accommodations for international travellers and corporate patrons, ensuring they experience the best in comfort and service.

Sustainability at Its Core

In an era where sustainability is paramount, Yashobhoomi proudly holds the prestigious IGBC Platinum Rating for Green Building Excellence. This certification underscores our commitment to eco-friendly operations and sustainable design. Our facility incorporates state-of-the-art energy-efficient systems, advanced water conservation technologies, and robust waste management practices, all geared towards minimizing environmental impact and setting a precedent for future development.

State-of-the-Art Public Transport Connectivity

At Yashobhoomi, accessibility is unparalleled, featuring a robust public transport framework that enhances visitor experience:

  • Direct Access to the Airport Metro Express:Offering seamless connectivity to and from the airport.
  • Proximity to the Delhi-Jaipur Railway Line and Delhi Metro Blue Line:Facilitating transit for those traveling from within the city and beyond.
  • Major Roadways Connectivity:Including direct access to Urban Extension Road II (UER II) and the Dwarka Expressway.

To further accommodate high footfall, Yashobhoomi boasts sophisticated parking facilities for 34,808 vehicles, with 28,608 indoor spaces and 6,200 outdoor spaces, ensuring convenience and ease of access for all visitors.

An All-Encompassing Multifunctional Facility

Sprawled over an impressive 890,000 square meters, Yashobhoomi offers an exceptionally versatile environment, equipped with more than just exhibition halls and auditoriums. Central to the complex is a captivating 1 km-long artistic foyer, providing an aesthetically pleasing transition between exhibition and convention spaces. Visitors will also have convenient access to:

  • Entertainment Zones:Engaging opportunities for leisure and enjoyment.
  • Shopping Centres:Diverse retail experiences within reach.
  • 3,500 Hotel Rooms:A range of accommodations suitable for various needs.
  • Office Spaces and Meeting Facilities:Ideal for corporate gatherings and collaborative sessions.

Discover the Best Accommodation at Yashobhoomi: Elevate Your Experience

When visiting Yashobhoomi, India’s premier exhibition and convention centre, the choice of accommodation can significantly enhance your experience. Located in the heart of the vibrant Delhi NCR region, visitors are presented with a multitude of options designed to cater to various needs and preferences. Currently, you can select from an impressive inventory of 3,633 rooms in Aero City, alongside 1,357 rooms in the surrounding areas and another 1,473 rooms in Gurgaon, all situated within a convenient 10–15-minute drive.

As Yashobhoomi continues to expand, we are excited to announce that upon the completion of Phase 2, an additional 3,500 hotel rooms will be available within walking distance of the Yashobhoomi complex. This development will ensure that visitors have convenient access to both world-class facilities and the vibrant activities hosted at Yashobhoomi.

Experience Excellence with KINEXIN

At the helm of Yashobhoomi’s operations is KINEXIN Convention Management Pvt. Ltd., a distinguished joint venture formed by KINTEX, Korea’s largest MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) venue, and Esang Networks, Korea’s sole Public Employment Organization (PEO) listed on the stock market. Since being awarded the management bid by the Government of India in 2018, KINEXIN has set a benchmark for excellence in the management and operation of Yashobhoomi (IICC).

KINTEX, accounting for 40% of Korea’s total exhibition space, brings a wealth of experience and a proven track record in managing large-scale venues. The expertise of KINEXIN was pivotal in securing the opportunity to operate Yashobhoomi following a rigorous and competitive selection process.

Yashobhoomi (IICC) is unparalleled in Delhi NCR, boasting direct access to Indira Gandhi International Airport—an essential hub welcoming over 54 million passengers annually. This proximity not only enriches visitor convenience but also positions Yashobhoomi as a prime location for global exhibitions, conventions, and tourism activities.

For comprehensive information about accommodations and upcoming events, we invite you to explore our official websites:

  • IICC Ltd (Yashobhoomi): https://iiccl.dpiit.gov.in/
  • Kinexin Official Venue Operator: https://www.iiccnewdelhi.com/

We look forward to welcoming you to Yashobhoomi, where every visit becomes a memorable experience!

Industrial Development Scheme (IDS), 2017 for Industrial Development in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

  • The Government of India launched the Industrial Development Scheme (IDS), 2017 to accelerate industrialization in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The Scheme was notified on 23rd April 2018 with a financial outlay of Rs 445.41 crore, covering the period 15th June 2017 to 31st March 2021, with provisions for continuation of benefits to meet committed liabilities.
  • IDS aims to address structural constraints such as high logistics costs and limited infrastructure by providing targeted fiscal support and improving the overall investment climate. The Scheme provides a focused push to both manufacturing and service sectors, enabling new investments as well as expansion of existing units.
  • The Scheme offers a comprehensive incentive framework including support for capital investment, interest on working capital, GST reimbursement, transport costs, insurance coverage, income tax reimbursement, and employment generation.   • A total of 380 industrial units have been granted registration under the Scheme, comprising 349 units in Jammu and Kashmir and 31 units in Ladakh, contributing to industrial growth through increased investments, expansion of productive capacity, and strengthening of the regional industrial ecosystem.
  • Overall, IDS serves as a catalyst for regional transformation by fostering entrepreneurship, strengthening industrial capacity, and promoting balanced and sustainable economic development in geographically challenging regions.

  • The Scheme provides a focused push to both manufacturing and service sectors, enabling new investments as well as expansion of existing units.

acf_data.scheme_title: North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007
acf_data.introduction: The Government has approved a package of fiscal incentives and other concessions for the North East Region namely the ‘North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007’, effective from 01.04.2007
acf_data.l3_introduction:
NOTIFICATION :-

NEIIPP, 2007 was notified on 01.04.2007 on revision of erstwhile North East Industrial Policy (NEIP), 1997.

COVERAGE :-

Eight North East States recognized under North Eastern Council (NEC)

ELIGIBILITY & DURATION:-

 All new units as well as existing units which go for industrial expansion located anywhere in North Eastern Region, which commence commercial production within 10 years period from the date of notification of NEIIPP, 2007 will be eigibile for incentives for a period of 10 years from the date of commercial production.

Exception are the industries considered hazardous to public health and environment such as tobacoo and its substitutes, pan masala, plastics carry bags of less than 20 microns, refinery products etc.

In addition to manufacturing sector, the benefits under NEIIPP, 2007 have for the first time, been extended to service sector, (i.e. Hotels not below Two Star category, adventure and leisure sports including ropeways, nursing homes with a minimum capacity of 25 beds, old-age homes, Vocational training institutes such as institutes for hotel management, catering and food crafts, entrepreneurship development, nursing and para-medical, civil aviation related training, fashion, design and industrial training, Bio-technology industry and Power Generating Industries-upto 10 MW).

Since Inception, Rs.3635.45 crore has been released to the states of NER till 31st July, 2023. During the Financial Year 2022-23, an amount of Rs.109.97 crore had been released to the states of NER. In the current FY 2023-24, there is a provision of Rs.200.00 crore in BE under NEIIPP, 2007 of which Rs110.23 crore had already been released till 31.07.2023..

SUBSIDY SCHEMES:-

 The subsidy schemes under NEIIPP, 2007 and their salient features and performance are given below :-

  1. Central Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme:-This scheme provides for Capital Investment Subsidy @ 30% of the value of plant and machinery, without any upper ceiling. The limit of automatic approval of subsidy is Rs.1.50 Crore; Rs.1.50 Crore to Rs.30 Crore with the approval of Empowered Committee and above Rs.30 Crore with the approval of the Union Cabinet.
  2. Central Interest Subsidy Scheme:-This scheme provides for an Interest Subsidy @ 3% on working capital loan taken by an industrial unit. This loan is provided for a maximum period of 10 (ten) years from the date of commencement of commercial production.
  3. Central Comprehensive Insurance Subsidy Scheme:-This scheme provides for 100% reimbursement of insurance premium paid by an industrial unit.

OTHER INCENTIVES/CONCESSIONS:-

  • Excise duty exemption based on “Value addition” norms specified by the Department of Revenue.
  • 100% Income Tax exemption.

COORDINATION AND MONITORING:-

 Various committees like High Level Committee, Advisory Committee along with over-sight Committee have been set up for proper Coordination and monitoring of NEIIPP, 2007.

NODAL AGENCY:-

 The North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd. (NEDFi), Guwahati is the designated agency for disbursal of subsidies under various subsidy schemes of NEIIPP, 2007.

acf_data.scheme_title: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods
acf_data.introduction: The scheme targets manufacturers of components / sub-assemblies of Air Conditioners & LED Lights and offers 4–6% incentive on incremental sales to boost localization, reduce imports, and build a domestic supply chain.
acf_data.l3_introduction:
The scheme targets manufacturers of components / sub-assemblies of Air Conditioners & LED Lights and offers 4–6% incentive on incremental sales to boost localization, reduce imports, and build a domestic supply chain.

(a) Details

Objective & Scope
The objective is to boost domestic manufacturing, reduce import dependence, build a strong component ecosystem for white goods, and position India in the global supply chain.
The scheme targets companies that invest in manufacturing components or sub-assemblies for:

  • Air Conditioners (ACs) — e.g. compressors, copper tubes, heat exchangers, motors, control assemblies, etc.
  • LED Lights — e.g. LED chips & packaging, LED drivers, LED engines, light-management systems, and other components in the LED-light value chain.

Implementation Period & Financial Outlay

  • The scheme runs from FY 2021-22 to FY 2028-29
  • Total approved outlay is Rs 6,238 crore.
  • Incentives under the scheme are provided for a period of 5 years on incremental sales (after one / two year gestation period), over the base year.

(b) Benefits

  1. Eligible companies get financial incentives ranging from 4% to 6% — on net incremental sales of goods manufactured in India under the scheme.
  2. The goal is to significantly raise domestic value addition — from existing ~15–20% to ~75–80%.
  3. Large incremental production and exports of AC & LED components.
  4. Creation of substantial employment (direct + indirect) across manufacturing ecosystem.
  5. Development of a complete “component-to-final-product” ecosystem, reducing dependence on imports.

(c) Eligibility

  1. Incentive under the Scheme shall be provided to Companies making brown field or green field Investments for manufacturing in target segments in India.
  2. Eligibility shall be subject to achievement of thresholds of net incremental sales of Eligible Products for the respective financial year over the base year or net incremental sales of eligible products over the base year or FY 2020-21, whichever is higher, as the case may be and cumulative incremental investment in the preceding financial year, which shall not be less than the threshold investment as detailed in Appendix-I or Appendix IA of the Scheme Guidelines, as the case may be.
  3. In case an applicant does not meet criteria of threshold investment and threshold net incremental sales for any given year, the applicant shall not be eligible for disbursement of incentive for that particular financial year. However, the applicant will not be restricted from claiming incentive for subsequent years during the tenure of the Scheme, provided eligibility criteria of cumulative committed investment and threshold net incremental sales are met for such subsequent financial years.
  4. The incremental sales of eligible products should be commensurate with created production capacity from investments committed under the scheme.
  5. For the purpose of determining eligibility of an applicant with respect to incremental investment, the investment covered under any other PLI Scheme of Govt. of India of the Applicant shall not be considered for determining eligibility under this PLI Scheme and vice-versa.
  6. In every financial year for which the incentive is claimed, the net sales turnover of eligible products of the selected applicant and its group companies shall not be less than the sum of their net sales turnover of eligible products manufactured in India in the base year for applicants meeting the pre-qualification criteria on the basis of financial attributes of base year and higher of net sales turnover of eligible products in the base year or FY 2020-21, for applicants meeting the pre-qualification criteria on the basis of financial attributes of FY 2020-21; along with the corresponding threshold incremental net sales turnover of the selected applicant as detailed in Appendix-1 or Appendix-IA of the Scheme Guidelines, as the case may be.
  7. For applicants opting for initial investment period as 1st April, 2021 to 31st March, 2023, the first and last year of achieving the required corresponding threshold incremental sales for availing the PLI shall be FY 2023-2024 and FY 2027-28 respectively as detailed in Appendix -IA of the Scheme Guidelines.

acf_data.introduction: Government of India is developing various Industrial Corridor Projects as part of National Industrial Corridor programme which is aimed at development of futuristic industrial cities in India which can compete with the best manufacturing and investment destinations in the world.
acf_data.l3_introduction:
1.1 National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) has been envisaged on the backbone of major transportation corridors like Eastern & Western Dedicated Freight Corridors, Expressways and National Highways, proximity to ports, airports, etc. and is aimed at development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities.

1.2 Objectives of the Corridor development is to

  1. Expand the industrial output,
  2. Increase employment opportunities,
  3. Provide better living and social facilities for the new and growing workforce,
  4. Providing ‘plug n play’ infrastructure at the plot level and to facilitate the manufacturing investments into the country by providing quality, reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure for the industries,
  5. By leveraging the multi-modal connectivity infrastructure that has developed in the last decade e.g, national highways, dedicated freight corridors, ports and airports, use of PM-GatiShakti to arrive at optimal locations for these cities by ensuring minimum logistic cost.

1.3 The development framework is based on a partnership approach between Government of India (GoI), which provides funds as equity/debt for development of trunk infrastructure and the respective State Governments, which provide lands for the same.

1.4 As part of NICDP, 11 Industrial corridors are being taken up for development. So far, the GoI has approved 20 industrial corridor projects (incl. 12 new projects approved in Aug,2024) across 13 states along 7 industrial corridors. acf_data.introduction: Discover endless possibilities for your business growth with NCSS, a dynamic government initiative committed to fueling the engines of entrepreneurship and industrial development in Jammu & Kashmir. Our mission is to empower businesses with the financial support they need to thrive and succeed.
acf_data.l3_introduction:
• The Government of India notified NCSS on 19th February 2021 to drive structural transformation of the industrial ecosystem in Jammu and Kashmir. With a financial outlay of Rs 28,400 crore, the Scheme aims to attract investments, support both new and existing units, and generate employment through a focused industry and services led development approach.
  • The Scheme is operational for the period 1st April 2021 to 31st March 2037. Units are required to commence production within 3 years from the date of registration, with eligible investments considered for those made on or after 1st April 2019.
  • NCSS is designed to address regional constraints through a comprehensive and incentive driven framework that promotes entrepreneurship, facilitates expansion, and improves ease of doing business. It focuses on job creation, skill development, and sustainable growth, while strengthening manufacturing and service sectors.
  • The Scheme provides four core incentives namely capital investment incentive (CII), capital interest subvention (CIS), GST linked incentive (GLI), and working capital interest subvention (WCIS), along with defined eligibility conditions such as minimum investment thresholds for service sector units.
  • Overall, NCSS positions Jammu and Kashmir as an investor friendly and competitive industrial destination by combining targeted financial support with a long-term policy framework for inclusive and resilient economic development.

acf_data.introduction: The Scheme of Budgetary Support under Goods and Services Tax Regime to the eligible units located in States of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, North East including Sikkim, Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir and Union Territory of Ladakh’ was notified on 5th October, 2017 by DPIIT.
acf_data.l3_introduction:
In 2017, the Government of India abolished the Excise regime and introduced Goods & Services Tax w.e.f. 01.07.2017. Under Central Goods and Services Act, 2017, all entities have to pay GST irrespective of exemption granted under then existing incentive scheme. The Scheme of Budgetary Support under Goods and Services Tax Regime to the eligible units located in States of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, North East including Sikkim, Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir and Union Territory of Ladakh’ was notified on 5th October, 2017 by DPIIT. The approved financial outlay of the scheme is Rs. 27,413 crore. It is a Central Government scheme, which is offered as a measure of goodwill in order to help the Units in their transition from erstwhile Excise regime to new GST regime. It envisages reimbursement of claims of only those Units which were eligible for drawing benefits under the earlier Excise Duty Exemption/refund schemes but it has otherwise no relation to the erstwhile Schemes.

With progressive de-licensing of industries, DPIIT now administers the compulsory licensing process under the IDR Act, 1951 for the following four industries: – (a) Electronic aerospace and defence equipment (b) Industrial explosives (c) Specified hazardous chemicals (d) Cigars and cigarettes of tobacco and manufactured tobacco substitutes.

Industrial license Services – All applications for Industrial License under IDR Act, 1951 and Arms Act, 1959 can now be applied online on NSWS Portal in their respective forms.

  1. The Applications are scrutinized for their completeness. Information in respect of incomplete applications is sought from the applicants.
  2. If the applications for grant of licence are complete in all respect with necessary documents, DPIIT circulates them to concerned administrative ministries, Ministry of Home Affairs, Concerned State Government and other concerned agencies for their comments.
  3. After receipt of comments from the concerned Ministries/Agencies, files are processed and submitted to the Licensing committee for consideration. Licensing Committee Meetings are held twice every month on every 01st and 03rd Thursday.
  4. Licensing committee can recommend for grant of licence/rejection of proposal/deferment of the proposal, based on the comments received and deliberations in the Committee. After recommendation, the approval of the Minister in charge of DPIIT is obtained for grant of licences or otherwise.
